claim: Conduction velocity is the speed at which electrical signals travel along axons and is a crucial determinant of neural communication.
source: Conduction velocity is the speed at which electrical signals travel along axons and is a crucial determinant of neural communication.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about neural communication.

claim: Inferences about conduction velocity can now be made in vivo in humans using a measure called the magnetic resonance (MR) g-ratio.
source: Inferences about conduction velocity can now be made in vivo in humans using a measure called the magnetic resonance (MR) g-ratio.
evidence: This is supported by citations to methodological papers throughout the manuscript.

claim: The MR g-ratio is the ratio of the inner axon diameter relative to that of the axon plus the myelin sheath that encases it.
source: This is the ratio of the inner axon diameter relative to that of the axon plus the myelin sheath that encases it.
evidence: This is a definition supported by Figure 1 showing the anatomical relationship.

claim: Variations in MR g-ratio of the parahippocampal cingulum bundle were associated with autobiographical memory recall ability in 217 healthy adults.
source: we found that variations in MR g-ratio, and by inference conduction velocity, of the parahippocampal cingulum bundle were associated with autobiographical memory recall ability in 217 healthy adults.
evidence: This is the primary finding supported by statistical analysis of data collected in the study.

claim: The parahippocampal cingulum bundle connects the hippocampus with a range of other brain areas.
source: This tract connects the hippocampus with a range of other brain areas.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge cited in the manuscript.

claim: The association between MR g-ratio and autobiographical memory recall seemed to be with inner axon diameter rather than myelin content.
source: We further observed that the association seemed to be with inner axon diameter rather than myelin content.
evidence: This is inferred from the pattern of correlations observed in the data and theoretical modeling.

claim: The extent to which neurites were coherently organised within the parahippocampal cingulum bundle was linked with autobiographical memory recall ability.
source: The extent to which neurites were coherently organised within the parahippocampal cingulum bundle was also linked with autobiographical memory recall ability.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of neurite orientation dispersion index data.

claim: The findings were specific to autobiographical memory recall and were not apparent for laboratory-based memory tests.
source: Moreover, these findings were specific to autobiographical memory recall and were not apparent for laboratory-based memory tests.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analyses showing no significant relationships with laboratory memory tests.

claim: Faster axonal conduction velocity is hypothesised to underpin the greater cognitive processing ability of vertebrates, in particular primates and humans, compared to invertebrates.
source: For example, an increase in axonal conduction velocity is hypothesised to underpin the greater cognitive processing ability of vertebrates, in particular primates and humans (Brancucci, 2012; Miller, 1994), compared to invertebrates (Arancibia-Cárcamo et al., 2017; Bullock et al., 1984; Nave, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: In rats and cats, faster axonal conduction velocity has been observed in younger compared to older animals.
source: In rats (Aston-Jones et al., 1985) and cats (Xi et al., 1999), faster axonal conduction velocity has been observed in younger compared to older animals.
evidence: This is supported by citations to specific animal studies.

claim: Axonal degradation that can lead to reduced conduction velocity has been identified in older compared to younger monkeys.
source: In a similar vein, axonal degradation that can lead to reduced conduction velocity has been identified in older compared to younger monkeys (Peters et al., 2000; Peters and Sethares, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to primate studies.

claim: Estimates of conduction velocity in humans from visual evoked potentials have been positively correlated with nonverbal intelligence quotients.
source: Echoing these findings from non-humans, estimates of conduction velocity in humans from the latency of visual evoked potentials recorded over primary visual cortex (Reed and Jensen, 1992) and between the thalamus and parietal cortex (Reed and Jensen, 1993) have been positively correlated with nonverbal intelligence quotients.
evidence: This is supported by citations to human electrophysiology studies.

claim: Faster axonal conduction velocities are thought to better explain increases in intelligence compared to absolute and relative brain volumes.
source: In addition, faster axonal conduction velocities are thought to better explain increases in intelligence compared to absolute and relative brain volumes (Dicke and Roth, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a theoretical paper.

claim: The conduction velocity of an axon is dependent upon the axon diameter, the presence and thickness of a myelin sheath, the distance between the nodes of Ranvier, inter-nodal spacing, and electrical properties of the axonal and myelin membranes.
source: The conduction velocity of an axon is dependent upon the axon diameter, the presence and thickness of a myelin sheath, the distance between the nodes of Ranvier (periodic gaps in the myelin that facilitate action potential propagation), inter-nodal spacing, and electrical properties of the axonal and myelin membranes (Arancibia-Cárcamo et al., 2017; Drakesmith et al., 2019; Gasser and Grundfest, 1939; Hursh, 1939; Huxley and Stampfli, 1949; Rushton, 1951).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple historical and contemporary citations.

claim: A larger axon diameter results in less resistance to the action potential ion flow, resulting in faster conduction velocity.
source: These two metrics are particularly key because a larger axon diameter results in less resistance to the action potential ion flow, resulting in faster conduction velocity.
evidence: This is established biophysical knowledge about axonal properties.

claim: The myelin sheath acts like an electrical insulating layer, reducing ion loss and preserving the action potential.
source: First, the myelin sheath acts like an electrical insulating layer, reducing ion loss and preserving the action potential.
evidence: This is established knowledge about myelin function.

claim: The presence of unmyelinated gaps in the myelin sheath (the nodes of Ranvier) enables a process called saltatory propagation to take place.
source: Second, the presence of unmyelinated gaps in the myelin sheath (the nodes of Ranvier) enables a process called saltatory propagation to take place.
evidence: This is established knowledge about neural signal propagation.

claim: Until recently, g-ratio measurements were restricted to invasive studies in non-human animals.
source: Until recently, g-ratio measurements were restricted to invasive studies in non-human animals.
evidence: This is a statement about the historical limitations of the methodology.

claim: It is now possible to estimate the g-ratio in vivo in humans across the whole brain by combining diffusion MRI with quantitative structural MRI scans optimised to assess myelination.
source: However, by combining diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with quantitative structural MRI scans optimised to assess myelination (e.g. magnetisation transfer saturation; Weiskopf et al., 2013), it is now possible to estimate the g-ratio in vivo in humans across the whole brain (Drakesmith et al., 2019; Mohammadi et al., 2015; Mohammadi and Callaghan, 2021; Stikov et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple methodological citations.

claim: The MR g-ratio is an area-weighted ensemble average across a voxel of an underlying distribution of microscopic g-ratios of axons.
source: This is achieved by measuring an aggregate g-ratio, which is an area-weighted ensemble average across a voxel of an underlying distribution of microscopic g-ratios of axons (Stikov et al., 2015; West et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a technical description supported by citations.

claim: MR g-ratio estimates have been used to investigate white matter development, changes in the g-ratio during aging, and as a potential neuroimaging marker in patients with multiple sclerosis.
source: These MR g-ratio estimates have been optimised (Ellerbrock and Mohammadi, 2018; Jung et al., 2018; West et al., 2018) and used to investigate white matter development (Cercignani et al., 2017), changes in the g-ratio during aging (Berman et al., 2018), and as a potential neuroimaging marker in patients with multiple sclerosis (Yu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior applications of the method.

claim: The MR g-ratio has been found to associate well with estimates of axonal conduction velocity.
source: Of note, the MR g-ratio has been found to associate well with estimates of axonal conduction velocity (Berman et al., 2019; Drakesmith et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to validation studies.

claim: The identification of statistically significant relationships with the MR g-ratio can guide as to which of inner axon diameter or myelin thickness might be influencing variations in conduction velocity.
source: Given that the MR g-ratio encompasses information about the inner axon diameter and myelin thickness, the identification of statistically significant relationships with the MR g-ratio can also guide as to which of these two features might be influencing variations in conduction velocity (Caeyenberghs et al., 2016; Kaller et al., 2017; Lakhani et al., 2016; Waxman, 1980; Xin and Chan, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations and represents an inference approach.

claim: Measuring the MR g-ratio with conventional MRI scanners can be useful in guiding inferences about inner axon diameter in the context of conduction velocity.
source: Consequently, measuring the MR g-ratio with conventional MRI scanners can be useful in guiding inferences about inner axon diameter in the context of conduction velocity.
evidence: This is inferred from the practical limitations of ultra-strong gradient scanners.

claim: Only four ultra-strong gradient Connectom MRI scanners exist in the world.
source: However, only four ultra-strong gradient Connectom MRI scanners exist in the world.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the availability of specialized equipment.

claim: The hippocampus is central to the processing of autobiographical memories.
source: There is no doubt that the hippocampus is central to the processing of autobiographical memories, and hippocampal damage is linked with autobiographical memory impairments (McCormick et al., 2018; Scoville and Milner, 1957; Winocur and Moscovitch, 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by classic and contemporary citations.

claim: No consistent relationship between autobiographical memory recall ability and hippocampal grey matter volume or microstructure has been identified in healthy individuals.
source: However, no consistent relationship between autobiographical memory recall ability and hippocampal grey matter volume or microstructure has been identified in healthy individuals (Clark et al., 2020; Clark et al., 2021a; LePort et al., 2012; Maguire et al., 2003; Van Petten, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple prior studies.

claim: A distributed set of brain areas supports autobiographical memory recall along with the hippocampus, including the parahippocampal, retrosplenial, parietal and medial prefrontal cortices.
source: The hippocampus does not act alone, and functional neuroimaging studies have revealed that a distributed set of brain areas supports autobiographical memory recall along with the hippocampus, including the parahippocampal, retrosplenial, parietal and medial prefrontal cortices (Andrews-Hanna et al., 2014; Maguire, 2001; Spreng et al., 2009; Svoboda et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to functional neuroimaging studies.

claim: Three white matter pathways enable communication with the hippocampal region: the fornix, the uncinate fasciculus and the parahippocampal cingulum bundle.
source: Three white matter pathways in particular enable communication with the hippocampal region – the fornix, the uncinate fasciculus and the parahippocampal cingulum bundle.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge.

claim: The fornix is a major pathway in and out of the hippocampus and connects it to the orbital and medial prefrontal cortices, the basal forebrain, the anterior thalamus, the hypothalamus and the mammillary bodies.
source: The fornix (Figure 3A) is a major pathway in and out of the hippocampus and connects it to the orbital and medial prefrontal cortices, the basal forebrain, the anterior thalamus, the hypothalamus and the mammillary bodies (Aggleton et al., 2015; Croxson et al., 2005).
evidence: This is anatomical knowledge supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 3A.

claim: The uncinate fasciculus originates in the uncus, entorhinal and parahippocampal cortices and passes over the lateral nucleus of the amygdala, arcs around the Sylvian fissure, terminating in various locations throughout the prefrontal cortex.
source: The uncinate fasciculus (Figure 3B) originates in the uncus, entorhinal and parahippocampal cortices and passes over the lateral nucleus of the amygdala, arcs around the Sylvian fissure, terminating in various locations throughout the prefrontal cortex (Croxson et al., 2005; Von Der Heide et al., 2013).
evidence: This is anatomical knowledge supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 3B.

claim: The parahippocampal cingulum bundle links the hippocampus with the entorhinal, parahippocampal, retrosplenial and parietal cortices, as well as providing another route between the hippocampus and anterior thalamus.
source: The parahippocampal cingulum bundle (Figure 3C) links the hippocampus with the entorhinal, parahippocampal, retrosplenial and parietal cortices, as well as providing another route between the hippocampus and anterior thalamus (Bubb et al., 2018; Jones et al., 2013b).
evidence: This is anatomical knowledge supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 3C.

claim: The parahippocampal cingulum bundle links to the prefrontal cortex via its connections with other parts of the cingulum bundle.
source: It also links to the prefrontal cortex via its connections with other parts of the cingulum bundle.
evidence: This is anatomical knowledge about connectivity.

claim: The study examined 217 healthy young adults from the general population (109 females, 108 males; mean age of 29.0 years, SD = 5.60; age range 20-41 years).
source: To ensure an appropriate sample size and a wide range of autobiographical memory recall ability, we examined a large group of healthy young adults from the general population (n=217; 109 females, 108 males; mean age of 29.0 years, SD = 5.60; age was restricted to between 20 and 41 years to limit the possible effects of aging).
evidence: This describes the study sample characteristics.

claim: All participants underwent the Autobiographical Interview.
source: All participants underwent the widely-used Autobiographical Interview (Levine et al., 2002).
evidence: This describes the study procedure.

claim: The Autobiographical Interview is the gold standard in the field for measuring autobiographical memory recall ability.
source: This task, which is the gold standard in the field, provides a detailed metric characterising a person's ability to recall real-life past experiences, as well as providing a useful control measure.
evidence: This is a characterization of the task's status in the field.

claim: The mean number of internal details provided per memory was 23.95 (SD = 7.25; range = 4.60–44.60).
source: Across the participants, the mean number of internal details provided per memory was 23.95 (SD = 7.25; range = 4.60–44.60).
evidence: This is a descriptive statistic from the study data.

claim: The mean number of external details provided per memory was 5.35 (SD = 3.20; range = 0.8–17.40).
source: Across the participants, the mean number of external details provided per memory was 5.35 (SD = 3.20; range = 0.8–17.40).
evidence: This is a descriptive statistic from the study data.

claim: None of the biophysical measures from the fornix were significantly associated with autobiographical memory recall ability.
source: We first investigated the fornix and uncinate fasciculus. None of the biophysical measures from either tract were significantly associated with autobiographical memory recall ability.
evidence: This is a negative finding from the statistical analyses.

claim: None of the biophysical measures from the uncinate fasciculus were significantly associated with autobiographical memory recall ability.
source: We first investigated the fornix and uncinate fasciculus. None of the biophysical measures from either tract were significantly associated with autobiographical memory recall ability.
evidence: This is a negative finding from the statistical analyses.

claim: There was a significant positive association between the parahippocampal cingulum bundle MR g-ratio and the number of internal details (r(211) = 0.18, p=0.008, 95% CI=0.05, 0.29).
source: A significant positive association was observed between the parahippocampal cingulum bundle MR g-ratio and the number of internal details (Figure 5A; r(211) = 0.18, p=0.008, 95% CI=0.05, 0.29).
evidence: This is the primary positive finding from statistical analysis, shown in Figure 5A.

claim: There was no association between the parahippocampal cingulum bundle MR g-ratio and external details (r(211) = –0.09, p=0.17, 95% CI=−0.21, 0.019).
source: This relationship was specific to internal details, with no association evident for the external details control measure (Figure 5B; r(211) = –0.09, p=0.17, 95% CI=−0.21, 0.019).
evidence: This is a negative finding for the control measure, shown in Figure 5B.

claim: There was a significantly larger correlation between the MR g-ratio and internal details than for external details (mean r difference = 0.28 (95% CI=0.11, 0.45), z=3.21, p=0.0013).
source: Direct comparison of the correlations confirmed there was a significantly larger correlation between the MR g-ratio and internal details than for external details (Figure 5C; mean r difference = 0.28 (95% CI=0.11, 0.45), z=3.21, p=0.0013).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Variations in the conduction velocity of the parahippocampal cingulum bundle are associated with individual differences in autobiographical memory recall ability.
source: This suggests that variations in the conduction velocity of the parahippocampal cingulum bundle are associated with individual differences in autobiographical memory recall ability.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the MR g-ratio findings.

claim: The positive correlation between MR g-ratio and autobiographical memory recall highlights the potential relevance of inner axon diameter rather than myelin thickness in the context of g-ratio and conduction velocity.
source: The positive nature of the correlation highlights the potential relevance of inner axon diameter rather than myelin thickness in the context of g-ratio and conduction velocity (Figure 2A orange arrow, and Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the direction of the correlation and theoretical modeling shown in Figure 2.

claim: Magnetisation transfer saturation values of the parahippocampal cingulum bundle were not significantly related to internal details (r(211) = 0.00, p=1.0, 95% CI=−0.12, 0.12).
source: Magnetisation transfer saturation values were not significantly related to either internal (r(211) = 0.00, p=1.0, 95% CI=−0.12, 0.12), or external (r(211) = 0.14, p=0.048, 95% CI=−0.06, 0.30) details.
evidence: This is a negative finding from statistical analysis.

claim: Better autobiographical memory recall is more likely to be related to parahippocampal cingulum bundle axons having larger inner axon diameters rather than thicker myelin sheaths.
source: Overall, therefore, under the assumption that the significant relationship between the MR g-ratio and autobiographical memory recall ability is associated with faster conduction velocity, Rushton's model of conduction velocity would indicate that better autobiographical memory recall is more likely to be related to parahippocampal cingulum bundle axons having larger inner axon diameters rather than thicker myelin sheaths (see Figure 2A orange arrow, and Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the pattern of results and theoretical modeling.

claim: There was a significant negative correlation between the neurite orientation dispersion index and internal details (r(211) = –0.19, p=0.005, 95% CI=−0.32,–0.06).
source: Partial correlations revealed a significant negative correlation between the neurite orientation dispersion index (a small orientation dispersion index value indicates low dispersion) and internal details (Figure 6A; r(211) = –0.19, p=0.005, 95% CI=−0.32,–0.06).
evidence: This is a finding from statistical analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: There was no significant relationship between the neurite orientation dispersion index and external details (r(211) = 0.07, p=0.28, 95% CI=−0.05, 0.20).
source: This was again specific to internal details with no significant relationship between the neurite orientation dispersion index and external details (Figure 6B; r(211) = 0.07, p=0.28, 95% CI=−0.05, 0.20).
evidence: This is a negative finding for the control measure shown in Figure 6B.

claim: There was a significantly larger correlation between the neurite orientation dispersion index and internal details than for external details (mean r difference = 0.27 (95% CI=0.44, 0.10), z=3.13, p=0.0017).
source: Direct comparison of the correlations revealed a significantly larger correlation between the neurite orientation dispersion index and internal details than for external details (Figure 6C; mean r difference = 0.27 (95% CI=0.44, 0.10), z=3.13, p=0.0017).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Neurite density was not significantly related to internal details (r(211) = 0.04, p=0.60, 95% CI=−0.09, 0.16).
source: Neurite density was not significantly related to either internal (r(211) = 0.04, p=0.60, 95% CI=−0.09, 0.16), or external (r(211) = 0.01, p=0.93, 95% CI=−0.12, 0.13) details.
evidence: This is a negative finding from statistical analysis.

claim: When neurites in the parahippocampal cingulum bundle were less dispersed and thus more coherently organised, this was associated with better autobiographical memory recall.
source: Therefore, in addition to a higher MR g-ratio, when neurites in the parahippocampal cingulum bundle were less dispersed and thus more coherently organised, this was associated with better autobiographical memory recall.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the neurite dispersion findings.

claim: There were no significant associations between fornix or uncinate fasciculus MR g-ratios or magnetisation transfer saturation values and any of the laboratory-based memory tests.
source: There were no significant associations between fornix or uncinate fasciculus MR g-ratios or magnetisation transfer saturation values and any of the laboratory-based memory tests (see Appendix 1—table 5, Appendix 1—table 6 for full details, source data are available in Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a negative finding from statistical analyses.

claim: No relationships with the MR g-ratio or magnetisation transfer saturation values were evident for any laboratory-based memory task.
source: Finally, we tested for associations between the key microstructure measures and performance on the eight laboratory-based memory tasks. No relationships with the MR g-ratio or magnetisation transfer saturation values were evident for any task, even when using an uncorrected p < 0.05 threshold (Appendix 1—table 21, source data are available in Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a negative finding from statistical analyses.

claim: The parahippocampal cingulum bundle MR g-ratio, and by inference conduction velocity, was specifically associated with recall of autobiographical memories from real life rather than performance on the more constrained laboratory-based memory tests.
source: This suggests that the parahippocampal cingulum bundle MR g-ratio, and by inference conduction velocity, was specifically associated with recall of autobiographical memories from real life rather than performance on the more constrained laboratory-based memory tests.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the pattern of positive and negative findings.

claim: A larger inner axon diameter reduces resistance to action potential signals, enabling greater conduction velocities.
source: A larger inner axon diameter reduces resistance to action potential signals, enabling greater conduction velocities (Gasser and Grundfest, 1939; Hursh, 1939), and coherently organised fibres may decrease the distance signals need to travel, further reducing communication times (Salami et al., 2003; Steriade, 1995).
evidence: This is established biophysical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Coherently organised fibres may decrease the distance signals need to travel, further reducing communication times.
source: A larger inner axon diameter reduces resistance to action potential signals, enabling greater conduction velocities (Gasser and Grundfest, 1939; Hursh, 1939), and coherently organised fibres may decrease the distance signals need to travel, further reducing communication times (Salami et al., 2003; Steriade, 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The combination of larger inner axon diameter and coherently organised fibres might optimise a fibre bundle for faster communication, which may benefit autobiographical memory recall.
source: This combination of features might optimise a fibre bundle for faster communication, and this may benefit autobiographical memory recall.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the functional implications of the findings.

claim: The parahippocampal cingulum bundle directly connects the hippocampus, parahippocampal, retrosplenial and parietal cortices, the anterior thalamus and, through other subdivisions of the cingulum bundle, the medial prefrontal cortex.
source: The parahippocampal cingulum bundle directly connects the hippocampus, parahippocampal, retrosplenial and parietal cortices, the anterior thalamus and, through other subdivisions of the cingulum bundle, the medial prefrontal cortex.
evidence: This is anatomical knowledge about the tract's connectivity.

claim: The regions connected by the parahippocampal cingulum bundle are typically engaged during fMRI studies of autobiographical memory recall.
source: These regions are typically engaged during fMRI studies of autobiographical memory recall (Andrews-Hanna et al., 2014; Maguire, 2001; Spreng et al., 2009; Svoboda et al., 2006), and damage to them is often associated with autobiographical memory impairments (Berryhill et al., 2007; McCormick et al., 2018; Scoville and Milner, 1957; Vann et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to functional neuroimaging studies.

claim: Damage to the regions connected by the parahippocampal cingulum bundle is often associated with autobiographical memory impairments.
source: These regions are typically engaged during fMRI studies of autobiographical memory recall (Andrews-Hanna et al., 2014; Maguire, 2001; Spreng et al., 2009; Svoboda et al., 2006), and damage to them is often associated with autobiographical memory impairments (Berryhill et al., 2007; McCormick et al., 2018; Scoville and Milner, 1957; Vann et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to lesion studies.

claim: The retrosplenial and parahippocampal cortices are thought to provide visuospatial elements of autobiographical memories.
source: The retrosplenial and parahippocampal cortices are thought to provide visuospatial elements of autobiographical memories (Dalton and Maguire, 2017; Epstein and Higgins, 2007; Mullally and Maguire, 2011; Vann et al., 2009), while the medial prefrontal cortex may initiate autobiographical retrieval and support schema-guided recall (Gilboa and Marlatte, 2017; McCormick et al., 2018; McCormick et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to functional studies.

claim: The medial prefrontal cortex may initiate autobiographical retrieval and support schema-guided recall.
source: The retrosplenial and parahippocampal cortices are thought to provide visuospatial elements of autobiographical memories (Dalton and Maguire, 2017; Epstein and Higgins, 2007; Mullally and Maguire, 2011; Vann et al., 2009), while the medial prefrontal cortex may initiate autobiographical retrieval and support schema-guided recall (Gilboa and Marlatte, 2017; McCormick et al., 2018; McCormick et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to functional studies.

claim: The parahippocampal cingulum bundle is uniquely positioned as a transmission highway enabling information to reach the hippocampus, where memories can be reconstructed.
source: The parahippocampal cingulum bundle is, therefore, uniquely positioned as a transmission highway enabling this information to reach the hippocampus, where memories can be reconstructed (Bartlett, 1932; Hassabis and Maguire, 2007; Schacter et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an inference about the tract's functional role supported by citations about memory reconstruction.

claim: Larger inner axon diameters and coherently organised neurites could facilitate rapid information flow along the parahippocampal cingulum bundle leading to more memory elements being available simultaneously, which in turn may result in increased detail and better integration of a memory representation.
source: Larger inner axon diameters and coherently organised neurites could facilitate rapid information flow along the parahippocampal cingulum bundle leading to more memory elements being available simultaneously, which in turn may result in increased detail and better integration of a memory representation.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanistic explanation for the findings.

claim: Two previous studies were suggestive of a relationship between parahippocampal cingulum bundle fractional anisotropy and autobiographical memory recall.
source: Two such studies were suggestive of a relationship between parahippocampal cingulum bundle fractional anisotropy and autobiographical memory recall (Irish et al., 2014; Memel et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The current study's analyses of standard DTI parameters replicated previous results showing a relationship between parahippocampal cingulum bundle fractional anisotropy and autobiographical memory recall.
source: Our analyses of the standard DTI parameters, therefore, replicated these previous results.
evidence: This is a statement about replication of prior findings.

claim: Fractional anisotropy and other physical parameters lack biological specificity and cannot speak to questions concerning axonal conduction velocity.
source: In addition, fractional anisotropy and other physical parameters lack biological specificity (Jensen and Helpern, 2010; Jones et al., 2013a) and, consequently, they cannot speak to questions concerning axonal conduction velocity, which is our main interest here.
evidence: This is a methodological limitation supported by citations.

claim: Bilateral lesions that selectively compromise or sever the parahippocampal cingulum bundle in humans are not reported in the literature.
source: In a similar vein, we are not aware of any reports of bilateral lesions that selectively compromise or sever the parahippocampal cingulum bundle in humans.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of certain lesion studies.

claim: Bilateral lesions to the parahippocampal cingulum bundle would be predicted to adversely affect the ability to recall autobiographical memories.
source: Given our findings, we would predict that such lesions would adversely affect the ability to recall autobiographical memories.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the current findings.

claim: No significant relationships between any neuroimaging metrics of the fornix and autobiographical memory recall ability were evident in the large cohort of young healthy adults.
source: We also examined two such tracts, the fornix and the uncinate fasciculus, but in both cases no significant relationships between any of our neuroimaging metrics and autobiographical memory recall ability were evident in our large cohort of young healthy adults.
evidence: This is a negative finding from the study.

claim: No significant relationships between any neuroimaging metrics of the uncinate fasciculus and autobiographical memory recall ability were evident in the large cohort of young healthy adults.
source: We also examined two such tracts, the fornix and the uncinate fasciculus, but in both cases no significant relationships between any of our neuroimaging metrics and autobiographical memory recall ability were evident in our large cohort of young healthy adults.
evidence: This is a negative finding from the study.

claim: The absence of associations between autobiographical memory recall and both the MR g-ratio and magnetisation transfer saturation values of the fornix and uncinate fasciculus speaks against a proportional change in microstructure.
source: However, we found no associations between autobiographical memory recall and both the MR g-ratio and magnetisation transfer saturation values of the fornix and uncinate fasciculus, which speaks against this explanation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the pattern of negative findings.

claim: Unlike a previous study, the current study did not find a relationship between fornix fractional anisotropy and autobiographical memory recall ability, which may be due to the larger sample examined.
source: In terms of standard DTI parameters, unlike a previous study (Hodgetts et al., 2017), we did not find a relationship between fornix fractional anisotropy and autobiographical memory recall ability, which may be due to the larger sample that we examined.
evidence: This is a comparison with prior work and speculation about the reason for the difference.

claim: Both the fornix and parahippocampal cingulum bundle are vulnerable to partial volume effects.
source: Both the fornix and parahippocampal cingulum bundle are vulnerable to partial volume effects (Concha et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a methodological consideration supported by a citation.

claim: Steps were taken to ensure the data were extracted only from white matter voxels to mitigate partial volume effects.
source: However, to mitigate this issue we took steps to ensure the data were extracted only from white matter voxels (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes a methodological approach used in the study.

claim: Diffusion data are susceptible to distortions which can particularly affect the uncinate fasciculus.
source: Diffusion data are also susceptible to distortions which can particularly affect the uncinate fasciculus.
evidence: This is a known methodological limitation.

claim: A new technique was used to improve distortion correction in the uncinate fasciculus region.
source: We addressed this challenge by using a new technique that improves distortion correction in this region (Clark et al., 2021b).
evidence: This describes a methodological approach with citation.

claim: The absence of fornix findings could echo those relating to hippocampal volume, whereby the structure is involved in autobiographical memory recall and damage impedes retrieval, but microstructural variations have limited impact within the healthy adult population.
source: The absence of fornix findings in our study could echo those relating to hippocampal volume (Clark et al., 2020; Clark et al., 2021a), whereby the structure is widely acknowledged to be involved in autobiographical memory recall, and damage impedes retrieval (Aggleton et al., 2000; D'Esposito et al., 1995; Gaffan and Gaffan, 1991; Tsivilis et al., 2008), but microstructural variations have limited impact within the healthy adult population.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations.

claim: Unilateral uncinate fasciculus lesions do not seem to significantly impair performance on laboratory-based memory tests.
source: Regarding the uncinate fasciculus, unilateral lesions do not seem to significantly impair performance on laboratory-based memory tests (Papagno et al., 2011) or the recall of premorbid autobiographical memories (Levine et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to lesion studies.

claim: Unilateral uncinate fasciculus lesions do not seem to significantly impair the recall of premorbid autobiographical memories.
source: Regarding the uncinate fasciculus, unilateral lesions do not seem to significantly impair performance on laboratory-based memory tests (Papagno et al., 2011) or the recall of premorbid autobiographical memories (Levine et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to lesion studies.

claim: Bilateral uncinate fasciculus lesions are very rare in humans, but might result in greater memory impairment.
source: Bilateral uncinate fasciculus lesions are very rare in humans, but might result in greater memory impairment.
evidence: This is speculation based on the rarity of such lesions.

claim: Hippocampal-prefrontal connections may be better served by pathways other than the uncinate fasciculus, such as the fornix or parts of the cingulum bundle.
source: Alternatively, hippocampal-prefrontal connections may be better served by other pathways, for example, via the fornix or parts of the cingulum bundle.
evidence: This is speculation about alternative anatomical pathways.

claim: The findings were specific to the internal details of autobiographical memories, which reflect the episodicity of past experiences.
source: Our findings were not only specific to the parahippocampal cingulum bundle, but also to the internal details of autobiographical memories, which reflect the episodicity of past experiences.
evidence: This is a characterization of the specificity of the findings.

claim: The control measure of external details did not correlate with any white matter microstructure metrics.
source: By contrast, our control measure of external details, also from the same task but which concerns non-episodic information in the autobiographical memories, did not correlate with any white matter microstructure metrics.
evidence: This is a negative finding for the control measure.

claim: No relationships were identified between parahippocampal cingulum bundle microstructure and any of the eight laboratory-based memory tasks examined.
source: Moreover, no relationships were identified with any of the eight laboratory-based memory tasks examined, highlighting the specific nature of the relationship between parahippocampal cingulum bundle MR g-ratio and, by inference, conduction velocity, and autobiographical memory recall ability.
evidence: This is a negative finding emphasizing specificity.

claim: Vivid, detailed, multimodal, autobiographical memories may rely on inter-regional connectivity, particularly that supported by the parahippocampal cingulum bundle, to a greater degree than simpler, more constrained laboratory-based memory tests.
source: It may be that vivid, detailed, multimodal, autobiographical memories rely on inter-regional connectivity, particularly that supported by the parahippocampal cingulum bundle, to a greater degree than simpler, more constrained laboratory-based memory tests.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the specificity findings.

claim: An fMRI meta-analysis showed that recall of autobiographical memories and laboratory-based memory stimuli were associated with substantially different neural substrates.
source: This result aligns with previous work involving an fMRI meta-analysis which showed that recall of autobiographical memories and laboratory-based memory stimuli were associated with substantially different neural substrates (McDermott et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a meta-analysis.

claim: The findings add to the increasingly-recognised importance of studying real-world cognition in order to fully characterise brain-behaviour relationships.
source: More generally, our findings add to the increasingly-recognised importance of studying real-world cognition in order to fully characterise brain-behaviour relationships (Maguire, 2001; Maguire, 2012; Miller et al., 2022; Mobbs et al., 2021; Nastase et al., 2020; Spiers and Maguire, 2007).
evidence: This is a broader implication supported by citations.

claim: Age, gender, scanner and the number of voxels within an ROI were included as covariates in all analyses.
source: Age, gender, scanner and the number of voxels within an ROI were included as covariates in all analyses, limiting the potential confounding effects of these variables.
evidence: This describes the statistical approach used.

claim: Analyses were performed using weighted means from each of the three white matter tracts of interest rather than voxel-wise across the whole brain, reducing the potential for false positives.
source: Our analyses were also performed using weighted means from each of the three white matter tracts of interest rather than voxel-wise across the whole brain, reducing the potential for false positives (Marek et al., 2022).
evidence: This describes the analytical approach with citation supporting the rationale.

claim: A sample of over 200 participants has been suggested as sufficient for correlational neuroimaging research.
source: We also tested a sample of over 200 participants, which has been suggested as sufficient for correlational neuroimaging research such as that performed here (Cecchetti and Handjaras, 2022; DeYoung et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to methodological papers.

claim: Relationships with autobiographical memory recall ability were specific to the MR g-ratio, and were not evident for any of its components, suggesting that it is the combination of these measures that is meaningful rather than any single measure alone.
source: Relationships with autobiographical memory recall ability were also specific to the MR g-ratio, and were not evident for any of its components (magnetisation transfer saturation, neurite density or isotropic volume fraction), suggesting that it is the combination of these measures, in the form of the MR g-ratio, that is meaningful rather than any single measure alone.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the pattern of findings.

claim: The MR g-ratio is an area-weighted average of all microscopic axons in an MRI-voxel that is slightly weighted towards larger axons.
source: First, the MR g-ratio is an area-weighted average of all microscopic axons in an MRI-voxel that is slightly weighted towards larger axons.
evidence: This is a technical description of the measure.

claim: MR proxies are required to estimate myelin and axonal volumes for the calculation of the MR g-ratio.
source: Second, MR proxies are required to estimate myelin and axonal volumes for the calculation of the MR g-ratio.
evidence: This is a methodological description.

claim: Multiple methodologies are available to estimate myelin and axonal volumes, with no consensus yet reached as to the best combination.
source: Multiple methodologies are available to estimate myelin and axonal volumes, with no consensus yet reached as to the best combination (Mohammadi and Callaghan, 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of the field supported by a citation.

claim: A calibration step is required to more closely align the MR proxies with the estimated volume fractions.
source: Third, a calibration step is required to more closely align the MR proxies with the estimated volume fractions.
evidence: This is a methodological description.

claim: The study used the standard single-point calibration method to estimate the slope of the myelin-based proxy, assuming that the offset can be neglected.
source: Here, we used the standard single-point calibration method to estimate the slope of the myelin-based proxy, assuming that the offset can be neglected.
evidence: This describes the specific calibration approach used.

claim: Future work may be able to improve MR g-ratio calibrations, and any calibration improvements would likely serve to increase the observed correlation.
source: Future work may be able to improve these calibrations. But, of note, since a non-negligible offset in the myelin-based proxy can increase the error in the MR g-ratio, any calibration improvements would likely serve to increase the observed correlation.
evidence: This is speculation about future methodological improvements.

claim: Although the model of the MR g-ratio allows for fibre dispersion, this is not accounted for in mapping to conduction velocity.
source: Fourth, although the model of the MR g-ratio allows for fibre dispersion (Stikov et al., 2015), this is not accounted for in mapping to conduction velocity.
evidence: This is a methodological limitation with citation.

claim: More advanced models may help to further elaborate on the relationships between MR g-ratio and conduction velocity in the future.
source: Going forward, more advanced models may help to further elaborate on these relationships.
evidence: This is speculation about future methodological developments.

claim: The myelin measure can be influenced by any factor, cognitive or demographic, that leads to a difference in absolute myelination.
source: Fifth, our myelin measure can be influenced by any factor, cognitive or demographic, that leads to a difference in absolute myelination.
evidence: This is a methodological consideration.

claim: The MR g-ratio is less affected by factors influencing absolute myelination because it is a relative measure and depends on the balance between absolute myelin and axonal volumes.
source: The MR g-ratio, however, is less affected by this limitation because it is a relative measure and does not depend on absolute myelin content but on the balance between absolute myelin and axonal volumes.
evidence: This is an explanation of an advantage of the MR g-ratio measure.

claim: The inference that the positive correlation between the MR g-ratio and autobiographical memory recall ability is potentially related to inner axon diameter is based upon Rushton's (1951) model rather than direct measurements of axon diameter.
source: Finally, our inference suggesting that the positive correlation between the MR g-ratio and autobiographical memory recall ability is potentially related to inner axon diameter is specifically in the context of g-ratio and conduction velocity, and is based upon Rushton's (1951) model rather than direct measurements of axon diameter.
evidence: This clarifies the basis for the inference and its limitations.

claim: The use of Connectom MRI scanners and more advanced biophysical models may be able to expand upon the relationship between MR g-ratio and inner axon diameter in the future.
source: The use of Connectom MRI scanners (Jones et al., 2018) and more advanced biophysical models may be able to expand upon this relationship in the future.
evidence: This is speculation about future research possibilities with citation.

claim: The parahippocampal cingulum bundle comprises both long and short association fibres with differing connectivity.
source: While we examined the parahippocampal cingulum bundle as a unitary pathway, it comprises both long and short association fibres with differing connectivity (Bubb et al., 2018).
evidence: This is anatomical knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Some fibres in the parahippocampal cingulum bundle form long range connections between the hippocampus and retrosplenial cortex, whereas others make shorter range connections between neighbouring regions.
source: Some fibres will form long range connections between, for example, the hippocampus and retrosplenial cortex, whereas others will make shorter range connections between neighbouring regions.
evidence: This is anatomical knowledge about the tract's organization.

claim: Connectom MRI is starting to make examination of short range 'u-fibres' possible in vivo in humans.
source: Connectom MRI is starting to make examination of short range 'u-fibres' possible in vivo in humans (Movahedian Attar et al., 2020; Shastin et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent technical developments.

claim: Future studies using Connectom MRI could seek to identify specific connections within the parahippocampal cingulum bundle that relate to individual differences in autobiographical memory recall.
source: While there are currently only four of these scanners in the world, future studies using Connectom MRI could seek to identify specific connections within the parahippocampal cingulum bundle that relate to individual differences in autobiographical memory recall.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future research.

claim: White matter microstructure measures related to conduction velocity have the potential to provide novel insights into how the brain processes and integrates information.
source: In conclusion, white matter microstructure measures related to conduction velocity are now possible to derive in vivo in humans. This has the potential to provide novel insights into how the brain processes and integrates information (Berman et al., 2019; Drakesmith et al., 2019), deepening our understanding of the information flow that underpins critical cognitive functions such as autobiographical memory recall.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the broader implications supported by citations.

claim: The study examined 217 participants including 109 females and 108 males.
source: Two hundred and seventeen healthy people took part in the study, including 109 females and 108 males.
evidence: This describes the study sample.

claim: Participants had English as their first language and reported no history of psychological, psychiatric or neurological conditions.
source: Participants had English as their first language and reported no history of psychological, psychiatric or neurological conditions.
evidence: This describes inclusion criteria.

claim: People with vocations such as taxi driving, ship navigators, aeroplane pilots, or those with regular hobbies including orienteering, or taking part in memory sports and competitions, were excluded.
source: Consequently, people with vocations such as taxi driving (or those training to be taxi drivers), ship navigators, aeroplane pilots, or those with regular hobbies including orienteering, or taking part in memory sports and competitions, were excluded.
evidence: This describes exclusion criteria.

claim: Of approximately 2000 people who contacted the researchers, 23 were explicitly excluded based on having expertise on classic hippocampal tasks.
source: Of the approximately 2000 people who contacted us, 23 were explicitly excluded on this basis.
evidence: This describes the screening process.

claim: The study was approved by the University College London Research Ethics Committee (project ID: 6743/001).
source: All participants gave written informed consent and the study was approved by the University College London Research Ethics Committee (project ID: 6743/001).
evidence: This describes ethical approval.

claim: Three MRI scanners were used to collect the neuroimaging data, all Siemens Magnetom TIM Trio systems with 32 channel head coils located at the same neuroimaging centre.
source: Three MRI scanners were used to collect the neuroimaging data. All scanners were Siemens Magnetom TIM Trio systems with 32 channel head coils and were located at the same neuroimaging centre, running the same software.
evidence: This describes the imaging equipment.

claim: Diffusion-weighted images were collected using the multiband accelerated EPI pulse sequence developed by the Centre for Magnetic Resonological Research at the University of Minnesota.
source: Diffusion-weighted images were collected using the multiband accelerated EPI pulse sequence developed by the Centre for Magnetic Resonance Research at the University of Minnesota (R012a-c, R013a on VB17, https://www.cmrr.umn.edu/multiband/; Feinberg et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the imaging sequence with citations.

claim: The mean number of voxels in the parahippocampal cingulum bundle ROI was 129.11 (SD = 25.68).
source: The mean number of voxels in the parahippocampal cingulum bundle ROI was 129.11 (SD = 25.68), and the variance in number of voxels across individuals was accounted for in our analyses.
evidence: This is a descriptive statistic about the ROI.

claim: A corrected statistical threshold of p<0.017 was applied to account for testing across three main tracts of interest.
source: As before, a corrected statistical threshold of p<0.017 was applied (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the statistical approach.

claim: The mean MR g-ratio of the parahippocampal cingulum bundle was 0.647 (SD = 0.043).
source: Table 1 shows the summary statistics for the microstructure measures
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

claim: The mean magnetisation transfer saturation of the parahippocampal cingulum bundle was 0.959 (SD = 0.007).
source: Table 1 shows the summary statistics for the microstructure measures
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

claim: The mean neurite dispersion (ODI) of the parahippocampal cingulum bundle was 0.189 (SD = 0.038).
source: Table 1 shows the summary statistics for the microstructure measures
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

claim: The mean neurite density of the parahippocampal cingulum bundle was 0.480 (SD = 0.051).
source: Table 1 shows the summary statistics for the microstructure measures
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

claim: This is the first application of MR g-ratio to human cognition.
source: Here, in the first application to human cognition, we found that variations in the MR g-ratio specifically in the parahippocampal cingulum bundle were associated with individual differences in autobiographical memory recall ability in a large sample of healthy adults.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study.
